column1: uikit-choice-v1|clobberedtraits-negative|Our choice-row test checks the selected state on a fresh cell. Would it catch a refresh that wipes traits supplied by another feature? Strengthen the test to cover a selection change.|let row = cell(); configure(row); XCTAssertNotNil(row.nameLabel.text)

uikit-containers-v1|wrongspan-negative|The grid test passes even if looking up the covered portion of a spanning seat returns nil. Give us a regression test for the actual lookup, including an uncovered coordinate.|let grid = DataGrid(rows: 3, columns: 2); XCTAssertEqual(grid.accessibilityRowCount(), 3)

uikit-speed-v1|repeatedchange-negative|This test keeps passing when tapping the selected speed calls the playback engine again. Exercise the button and count actual change deliveries across two taps.|let panel = PlaybackSpeedChoices(); XCTAssertFalse(panel.buttons.isEmpty)

macos-navigation-v1|lostselection|CI only checks the table's size. It missed an invoice selection moving after a sort. Can you show how to catch that using equal titles and different identifiers?|let r = results(); r.select("b"); r.apply([b,a]); XCTAssertEqual(r.table.numberOfRows, 2)

tvos-results-v1|motionhidescontent|Our motion test checks only that the animation did not run. How do we catch the regression where the status never changes for people who enable Reduce Motion?|var calls = 0; let s = TelevisionStatus(reduceMotion: { true }, animate: { calls += 1 }); s.update("Ready"); XCTAssertEqual(calls, 0)

macos-structure-v1|selection|A Mac outline refresh passes our smoke test even when selection moves to a different sibling. Add a test that exercises the refresh with a real selection.|let d = configured(); XCTAssertGreaterThan(d.outline.numberOfRows, 0)

uikit-naming-v1|exposeddecoration-negative|The title is discoverable, yet our test would stay green if a purely decorative icon were also exposed. Strengthen the test for both elements after configuration.|let card = ItemActionCard(); configure(card); XCTAssertTrue(card.titleLabel.isAccessibilityElement)

uikit-modal-v1|earlynotification-negative|Our dismissal test inspects only the eventual notification count. It misses a focus request sent before the animation completion. Capture the intermediate state and check the final target.|let panel = RestoringPanel(), background = UIView(); XCTAssertTrue(open(panel, background: background))

macos-lifecycle-v1|original-responder-check|Opening our modal passes the test, but it never exercises refusal by the original responder. How would you check the fallback used on completion?|let h = ModalHarness(); _ = h.begin(); XCTAssertNotNil(h.fallback)

ios-closure-v1|validation-snapshot|Our validation test simulates an edit using only the controller's public edit method. What test would expose a stale success after a text field was changed directly?|let o = owner(); o.edit("name", "Original"); o.submit(); o.edit("name", "New"); XCTAssertEqual(o.snapshot["name"], "New")

uikit-contrast-v1|nolinearization-negative|Our contrast test covers only black against white. It still passes with the wrong luminance calculation. Add a numerical fixture whose expected value comes from outside the function under test.|XCTAssertEqual(try gray(0).contrast(with: gray(1)), 21, accuracy: 1e-12)

macos-appkit-v1|lostordinarysave|Our test checks that the row is recognizable, but Save has disappeared from the ordinary action path before. Add proof that operates the visible control and observes its callback.|XCTAssertEqual(row().title.stringValue, "Invoice A")

tvos-uikit-v1|lostordinarydetails|Our snapshot-level check sees a Details title even when pressing the control no longer invokes Details. Strengthen this at the actual primary-action entry point.|let r = row(); XCTAssertNotNil(r.details.title(for: .normal))

tvos-structure-v1|grouping|The shelf remains on screen even when its items disappear as independent accessibility targets. Update the unit check to distinguish the two structures.|let v = configured(); XCTAssertFalse(v.shelves.isEmpty)

macos-closure-details-v1|row-selected|The row still says “Report” after selection. The test passes even when the selected flag never changes. Can you exercise select and deselect while preserving the row's other semantics?|let r = DesktopRow(); r.configure(id: "one", title: "Report", selected: true, expanded: true); XCTAssertEqual(r.accessibilityLabel(), "Report")

uikit-dynamic-v1|missingelements-negative|Our rotor test checks only whether the search index accepted the initial data. It should detect a missing or misordered accessibility element after a reorder. Check the container and the rotor installed on the view.|let view = DynamicSections(frame: .zero); XCTAssertTrue(view.replace(records))

uikit-preferences-v1|ignoredmotion-negative|This timing assertion passes for every nonnegative duration. Can you make the check distinguish a reduced-motion transition from the ordinary transition?|XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(MotionPolicy.duration(reduceMotion: true), 0)

uikit-semantics-v1|losttraits-negative|We configured the bookmark twice and asserted only its label. Please exercise a trait owned by another feature through selection and deselection.|let button = UIButton(type: .system); SemanticConfiguration.configure(button, selected: true, hint: "Save"); XCTAssertEqual(button.accessibilityLabel, "Bookmark")

uikit-reuse-v1|staleidentity-negative|Our reuse test checks the new title and misses a retained Remove action affecting the replacement item. How would you exercise the originally installed action after the change?|let cell = SavedItemCell(); cell.configure(id: "2", title: "Hello", saved: false, removable: true, language: "en-US"); XCTAssertEqual(cell.titleLabel.text, "Hello")

uikit-lifecycle-v1|wrongnotification-negative|The motion test checks the initial value but never changes the preference. Can you drive the notification and verify the new value while ignoring an unrelated notification?|let center = NotificationCenter(); let model = MotionPreference(center: center) { false }; XCTAssertFalse(model.reduceMotion)
